model_name: Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512 (base checkpoint; audited as the official current 0.5B CosyVoice3 checkpoint)
exact_variant: Official model card is FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512. The official repo changelog says the base and RL variants were released in 2025/12. This audit refers to the base checkpoint (llm.pt), not the separate RL checkpoint (llm.rl.pt). The checkpoint family is labeled 0.5B; exact parameter count is not published/found.
parameter_count: 0.5B as the source-reported model-size class; exact parameter count not published/found.
reported_weight_size: No single deployable-checkpoint byte total is identified. Official HF API reports repository usedStorage=11,767,984,206 bytes (repository-level, not one checkpoint). Its file inventory lists, among others: llm.pt 2,024,669,519 bytes; llm.rl.pt 2,024,682,701 bytes (separate RL model); flow.pt 1,329,116,148 bytes; hift.pt 83,202,622 bytes; CosyVoice-BlankEN/model.safetensors 988,097,824 bytes; campplus.onnx 28,303,423 bytes; flow.decoder.estimator.fp32.onnx 1,326,216,933 bytes; speech_tokenizer_v3.onnx 969,451,503 bytes and speech_tokenizer_v3.batch.onnx 969,451,579 bytes. Repository includes distinct formats/variants, so do not sum as if all were simultaneously required. 54 GiB free disk exceeds the repository-level figure, but actual setup adds software/cache space.
text_description_voice_design: Natural-language-only speaker-description-to-new-voice design: not officially documented/found. The official example of inference_instruct2 supplies a prompt WAV as well as an instruction; its examples instruct language/dialect or speaking speed, not a new speaker identity from text alone. Do not treat this as text-only custom-voice design.
reference_audio_cloning: Supported. Official examples use inference_zero_shot/inference_instruct2 with a reference WAV (and transcription/prompt text); source describes multilingual/cross-lingual zero-shot voice cloning. This is reference-audio voice cloning, distinct from description-only voice design.
language_and_control_coverage: Official docs list Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, French, Italian and Russian, plus 18+ Chinese dialects/accents. They describe natural-language instruction control for language/dialect, emotion, speed and volume, as well as pronunciation inpainting, text normalization and streaming. These are source-stated capabilities, not independent validation of each control's quality.
code_license: Apache License 2.0 per the official repository LICENSE. This covers repository code; third-party dependencies may have their own licenses.
weights_license: Apache-2.0 is declared in the official Hugging Face checkpoint metadata (license: apache-2.0). This is separate from the code license; verify applicable terms for any included third-party artifacts independently.
cpu_memory_and_runtime_evidence: Official setup instructs Python 3.10 and gives Ubuntu/Linux dependency instructions; optional ttsfrd wheel is cp310 Linux. Python 3.12.3 is outside the documented setup, and compatibility is not established by these sources. No official CPU-only support statement, CPU/RAM minimum, or CPU throughput benchmark found; thus 8 cores/23 GiB RAM cannot be certified as sufficient or performant. No model-specific GPU minimum published/found; repository deployment examples use NVIDIA Docker, and vLLM/TensorRT paths have specific hardware/software requirements. CPU-only success/failure should not be inferred. No installation or model download was performed.
quality_ranking_evidence: no comparable public rank found. Voice Arena's fetched leaderboard and roster/methodology do not list CosyVoice3, so no TTS Arena rank/score is claimed. A published human MOS comparison is available in the CosyVoice3 paper (arXiv v2, 2025-05): in its cross-lingual voice-cloning Table 8, CosyVoice3-0.5B scores MOS 3.82 on en→zh and 3.75 on zh→en. Baselines: F5-TTS 3.77/3.77, Spark-TTS 3.65/3.61, CosyVoice2 3.87/3.75. These are task-specific MOS scores, not an overall leaderboard rank. Paper Table 4 also reports non-human-perception metrics on SEED-TTS-Eval (base 0.5B: zh CER 1.16%, speaker similarity 0.780 WavLM/0.840 ERes2Net; en WER 2.02%, SS 0.718/0.790; hard zh CER 6.08%, SS 0.758/0.815); not a global quality rank. Newer 2512 model-card table publishes a different evaluation table, but it likewise does not provide an overall listening rank.
github_popularity_evidence: Popularity is not quality. Official Hugging Face model API response fetched 2026-10-10 reports 161,540 downloads and 655 likes; time-sensitive popularity proxies only. No GitHub star count is asserted.
integration_notes: Official model card documents local Python use via cosyvoice.cli.cosyvoice.AutoModel and inference_zero_shot, inference_cross_lingual, and inference_instruct2. Repository has FastAPI/gRPC runtime examples, but these generic deployment examples are not evidence of an official hosted service or OpenAI-compatible API specifically for this checkpoint. Official quickstart pins Python 3.10; no documented Python 3.12 support found. Linux/Ubuntu setup is documented. CPU-only deployment instructions and minimum hardware are absent.
caveats: Audit is current through 2026-10-10; sources can change afterward.
The audited concrete checkpoint is the official 0.5B-2512 base variant, not the RL checkpoint or every earlier paper checkpoint.
Exact parameter count was not published/found; 0.5B is the stated size class, not an exact count.
The Hugging Face repository contains alternative/duplicate-format files; repository storage and individual file sizes are not a guaranteed minimal runtime footprint.
No official evidence settles CPU-only operability or RAM adequacy for the specified computer. Python 3.12 is not the documented Python 3.10 environment.
Official documentation examples for instruction control require reference audio; no description-only custom-speaker design mode was found.
Paper MOS figures are limited to the paper's cross-lingual cloning task and should not be interpreted as a broad comparative rank.
Popularity counters are a dated snapshot, not model quality evidence.
